samples.summary: Adding `readOnly` to the mount-effect deps makes the effect re-runnable, but the cleanup never disposes `YorkieDocStore` — the old store stays subscribed to the Yorkie doc and drives the DISPOSED editor (and publishes presence) on every remote change.
samples.evidence: `YorkieDocStore`'s constructor registers `doc.subscribe(...)` and discards the unsubscribe (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:622); the class has no `dispose()`/`unsubscribe` at all (grep over that file returns no matches). The effect cleanup (docs-view.tsx:549-571) unsubscribes presence and calls `editor.dispose()`, but only sets `storeRef.current = null` — it never clears `store.onRemoteChange` (installed at docs-view.tsx:410) nor tears down the store's own doc subscription. Before this delta the effect keyed on `[didMount, doc]` and effectively ran once per document, so the leak was unobservable. Now every `readOnly` transition builds a second `YorkieDocStore` while the first one lives on: on the next remote change the stale handler runs `editor.clearImageSelection()`, `editor.getDoc().refresh()`, `editor.restoreLocalCursor(...)`, `editor.render()` against the disposed editor (whose canvas was removed and whose measure caches were released at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4405-4412), and then `store.publishResolvedLocalCursor(...)` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1274-1286) writes presence through the RAW, un-read-only store — clobbering the live editor's caret broadcast with the stale one, from a session that may have just lost write authority. Fix belongs in the new code path: clear `store.onRemoteChange` and unsubscribe the store in the cleanup (or give `YorkieDocStore` a `dispose()`).

samples.summary: The new `readOnly` dep is inert at every current call site — no caller ever changes the prop — so the permission the comment says is now re-applied still never gets re-armed on a live session.
samples.evidence: Only two mounts of `DocsView` exist: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-detail.tsx:280` never passes `readOnly` (so it is permanently `undefined`), and `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:364` passes `resolved.role === "viewer"` (line 322), where `resolved` is set once by a single `resolveShareLink(token)` in `useEffect` keyed on `[token]` (shared-document.tsx:1086-1102) and is never refetched or polled. So the very scenario the new comment cites at docs-view.tsx:575-578 ("a share link re-resolving from `editor` to `viewer`") cannot occur, and the editor is still never rebuilt against a changed permission. Either a re-resolve/poll is missing upstream, or the comment overstates what the dep achieves.

samples.summary: `TextEditor`'s held-render contract requires the host to install `requestLayoutRefresh`; the second host, `initializeTextBox` (docs text boxes + every slides shape / text-box / table-cell editor), never does, so mid-unit reads of `getLayout()` see a pre-edit layout.
samples.evidence: `TextEditor.requestRender` defers the paint while an undo unit is open and calls `this.requestLayoutRefresh?.()` so the rest of the unit still reads a fresh layout (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:734-743, contract documented at text-editor.ts:3821-3827). The only assignment in the repo is packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2545 (the wrapper this delta rewrites). `initializeTextBox` constructs its `TextEditor` at packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:668-705 and sets `onComposingContextChange`, `setCursorTarget`, `onLinkRequest`, but never `requestLayoutRefresh`, so the optional call is a no-op there. Inside `insertText`'s unit (text-editor.ts:835-844) — the path this delta's new tests pin — `deleteSelection()` removes blocks and then `this.getWrapAffinity(newPos)` reads a layout still describing the pre-delete document, yielding a wrong caret affinity at a wrap boundary. It degrades rather than throws (getVisualLineRange's lookups are all optional, text-editor.ts:4739-4746), hence minor; the fix belongs in text-box-editor.ts (wire `requestLayoutRefresh` to its `layoutCache = undefined; recomputeLayout()` shim).

verdict.reason: All four elements of the finding check out in the repo. The mount effect now keys on `readOnly` (docs-view.tsx:581) and builds a new `YorkieDocStore` on each run (docs-view.tsx:356). `YorkieDocStore`'s constructor registers `doc.subscribe(...)` and discards the unsubscribe, firing `this.onRemoteChange?.()` on remote changes (yorkie-doc-store.ts:622-627); the class exposes no `dispose()`/unsubscribe (grep for dispose|unsubscribe in that file matches only the subscribe call). The effect cleanup (docs-view.tsx:549-571) unsubscribes only the view's own `"others"` subscription and calls `editor.dispose()`, leaving `store.onRemoteChange` (installed at docs-view.tsx:410-439) and the store's doc subscription intact. So after any `readOnly` transition the previous store still fires its handler, driving a disposed editor (canvas removed, measure caches released at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4405-4412) and calling `publishResolvedLocalCursor` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1274-1286) through the RAW, un-read-only store — read-only wrapping happens inside `initialize` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1075) — clobbering the live editor's presence. No guard prevents a second construction; `readOnly` is derived from async state in shared-document.tsx:322 with `SharedDocumentByToken` re-resolving on token change without unmounting (shared-document.tsx:1086-1102, template-review-queue.tsx:136). This is an out-of-diff invariant ("store constructed exactly once, never torn down") broken by the diff's new re-run path — squarely in the blast-radius lane, and major since the stale path corrupts presence and touches a disposed editor.

mergedFrom.summary: Wiring `requestLayoutRefresh = recomputeLayout` consumes `dirtyBlockIds`, so the deferred paint's own `recomputeLayout` runs cache-disabled — a full-document re-measure per edit

finding.summary: Wiring `requestLayoutRefresh = recomputeLayout` makes every batched edit relayout the WHOLE document a second time (the incremental dirty-block cache is consumed by the in-unit refresh)
finding.evidence: `recomputeLayout` ends by clearing the incremental state: `dirtyBlockIds = undefined` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1534), and `computeLayout` only uses the cache when `dirtyBlockIds != null` (`canUseCache = cache != null && dirtyBlockIds != null && …`, packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:456-459). New flow per edit: the interior `requestRender()` inside `withUndoUnit` calls `requestLayoutRefresh()` = `recomputeLayout` (editor.ts:2531) which consumes the dirty set, then the held render is replayed after the unit and `render()` (editor.ts:2208-2211) calls `recomputeLayout` again — now with `dirtyBlockIds === undefined`, so it re-measures and re-lays-out every body block plus header/footer instead of the one dirty block. Before this change each keystroke produced exactly one incremental pass. `handleInput` wraps *all* typing in a unit (text-editor.ts:1020), so ordinary typing becomes O(document) per keystroke — the same property editor.ts:2440-2444 says the caret path exists to preserve. Fix belongs on the new code: have the in-unit refresh preserve/repopulate `dirtyBlockIds` (or skip the second recompute), not on `recomputeLayout`'s callers.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise — that the diff wires `requestLayoutRefresh = recomputeLayout` directly, letting the in-unit refresh consume the incremental dirty set — is not the code in this repository. `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2545-2549` assigns a wrapper that saves and restores the state: `const dirty = dirtyBlockIds; recomputeLayout(); dirtyBlockIds = dirty ?? new Set();`. The two supporting facts are accurate (`recomputeLayout` clears `dirtyBlockIds` at editor.ts:1534; `canUseCache` requires `dirtyBlockIds != null` at layout.ts:456-459), but because the wrapper reinstates a non-null set, the deferred post-unit `render()` still takes the incremental cache path (layout.ts:535) rather than re-measuring every block. The mitigation the finding prescribes ("have the in-unit refresh preserve/repopulate dirtyBlockIds") is already implemented at the exact location it names, and documented in the comment at editor.ts:2532-2544 including the `undefined -> new Set()` case. Grep across all packages shows only one assignment of `requestLayoutRefresh` (declaration text-editor.ts:233, sole call site text-editor.ts:739), so no other wiring reintroduces the direct-handover shape. Hence no O(document)-per-keystroke regression follows.
